title: Bengal extends ISKCON-run mid-day meals from Kolkata to schools across the state
dek: A School Education Department notification brings all state-run and aided schools under PM POSHAN, with districts to be added in phases as central kitchens are set up.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal has authorised an ISKCON-linked kitchen network to supply mid-day meals to all state-run and state-aided schools in the state, extending statewide an arrangement that until now covered only schools in Kolkata.

The School Education Department issued the notification on Saturday evening, according to reports. It says the meals will be rolled out district by district in phases, not all at once, and that district administrations must identify suitable sites for central kitchens and help set them up. All the schools are being brought under the Centre's PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) scheme, which funds cooked meals for government school students. The government has not published the number of schools or students covered, the order in which districts will be added, or a start date.

## How the Kolkata arrangement works

The government of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari handed mid-day meals in Kolkata Municipal Corporation schools to an ISKCON-run kitchen on 1 August, when Mr Adhikari inaugurated a large central kitchen at Taratala. At the time the plan was to serve about 44,000 students in some 500 government and aided schools in the city, with a target of 2.5 lakh students within three months, according to reports. The state raised its allocation to Rs 10 per student per meal.

The ISKCON kitchens serve vegetarian food. After criticism that children would lose eggs from their diet, the government said women's self-help groups would continue to provide eggs separately. Reports on Saturday said the same system would apply across the state. Mr Adhikari said in August that no school cook would lose their job, and that cooks' monthly wages would rise from Rs 2,000 to Rs 3,000.

Reports have named different organisations as the operator. Some refer to the Annamrita Foundation, which has served Kolkata schools since August; others to the Akshaya Patra Foundation. Both are linked to ISKCON, although ISKCON has said in correspondence connected to a Calcutta High Court case that neither body is part of its governing structure.

## An earlier order withdrawn

This is the government's second attempt to take the scheme beyond Kolkata. On 11 September a joint secretary in the education department withdrew an order that had allowed the Akshaya Patra Foundation to serve meals under PM POSHAN in Howrah, Purulia, North 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur districts, according to reports. The government did not give a public reason at the time.

In the first weeks of the Kolkata rollout, some teachers complained that meals arrived late or not at all, and that teachers had to serve food delivered in bulk from the central kitchens, according to reports.

## What happens next

District officials will now have to find land for central kitchens, which will decide how quickly each district is added. It is not yet clear how the change will affect self-help groups that currently cook meals in schools outside Kolkata, or whether existing contracts will end. No reaction from opposition parties to the new notification had been reported by Saturday night.
